messages:
alex: Heads-up: I'm landing a terraform module refactor that hoists provider blocks to the root module and standardizes module inputs to v2.0.0. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3456. Tests looked fine locally but staging apply failed with a provider plugin mismatch. @tara any tips?

tara: hmm yea that's usually the lockfile. Did you update .terraform.lock.hcl in the PR?

alex: I committed the module source changes but didn't regenerate lockfile to avoid noise. The error was: 
```
Error: Inconsistent provider plugins
  on .terraform/plugins/plugins.json: provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws: version 4.39.0 expected, but 4.40.0 found
```

liam: quick fix: run `terraform init -upgrade -lockfile=write` in the root after hoisting providers. That will update .terraform.lock.hcl to match the new provider set.

tara: also watch for duplicate provider constraints across child modules. If child modules have explicit `required_providers`, they can collide when you hoist. Best to remove duplicate `required_providers` or relax child pins and keep root pinned.

sophia: FYI, the module source refs changed to `git::https://...//modules?ref=v2.0.0` — make sure the module tag includes the api change so state mapping stays consistent. If any module address changes you may need `terraform state mv`.

alex: good call. If we rename module addresses, what's the recommended state move command pattern?

liam: pattern: `terraform state mv module.old_name.module.some_resource module.new_name.module.some_resource` — run from the workspace with the current state. Do it in a maintenance window or as a separate step before full apply.

tara: if it's many resources, use a small script with `terraform state list` + `sed` to map names. I can share ours if you want.

alex: please share if it's quick. Also, any CI caveats? We saw a plan succeed in CI but apply failed in staging because staging used a cached plugin.

liam: CI runs `terraform init` in a clean container, but staging deploy nodes keep a plugin cache. Ensure deploy node runs `terraform init -upgrade` or clear plugin cache. Also tag the PR with `infra: lockfile` so automation knows to run lockfile checks.

infra-bot: plan for branch alex/refactor-modules completed — 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. (`plan_id=plan-20260314-778`)

tara: Alex — if you regenerate the lockfile and push, I can review and approve. Also check for any providers in `examples/` or test workspaces.

alex: Pushed updated .terraform.lock.hcl and a tiny state-mapping script in scripts/state-mv.sh. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3456/files. I'll wait for your review before running state moves.

tara: looking now. If everything looks good, I'll approve and schedule the apply in tonight's infra window. :+1:

alex: thanks! rolling forward after approvals, will post runbook before apply. :rocket:
